name: Dwarka Point
tower: 43 m (141 ft) square masonry tower with lantern and gallery, attached to a 1-story keeper's house/harbor control center
colors: Lighthouse painted with horizontal black and white bands
text: 1962 (station established 1866). Active; focal plane 48 m (157 ft); two white flashes every 20 s. 43 m (141 ft) square masonry tower with lantern and gallery, attached to a 1-story keeper's house/harbor control center. Lighthouse painted with horizontal black and white bands. A 2024 photo is at the top of this page, a 2018 photo is available, Elvin Lonan has a 2010 photo, Tanmay Vora has a 2008 photo, Wikimedia has a distant view, Harshang Chhaya has a closeup street view, and Google has a satellite view. This is the westernmost lighthouse of Saurashtra and a well-known tourist attraction. The original lighthouse, an 18 m (59 ft) square masonry tower, was built by the native state of Baroda. Located at the end of the peninsula sheltering the west side of the harbor of Dwarka. Site open, tower open daily. . ARLHS IND-133; Admiralty F0396; NGA 28300.

name: Kachhigadh
tower: 30 m (98 ft) round cylindrical concrete tower with lantern and gallery, painted with horizontal red and white bands
colors: tower with lantern and gallery, painted with horizontal red and white bands
text: 1983 (station established 1977). Active; focal plane 34 m (112 ft); four white flashes every 15 s. 30 m (98 ft) round cylindrical concrete tower with lantern and gallery, painted with horizontal red and white bands. Arvind Prajapati has the 2022 photo seen at right, Vatsal Mandavia has a closeup 2021 photo, Sejul Antala has a closeup, R. Ramesh has a street view from the nearby beach, and Google has a satellite view. The station was established with a temporary light on a "cabin" in 1977. It marks the southern approach to the Gulf of Kachchh (Kutch). Located about 15 km (9 mi) north of Dwarka. Site open, tower closed. ARLHS IND-142; Admiralty F0397; NGA 28304.

name: Mithapur
tower: 49.5 m (163 ft) building
text: Date unknown. Active; focal plane 53 m (174 ft); continuous red light. 49.5 m (163 ft) building. A giant Tata Chemicals plant dominates Mithapur and its main office building is almost certainly the location of the light. A photo is available and Google has a street view and satellite view. Mithapur is about 10 km (6 mi) southwest of Okha. Site open, tower closed. Admiralty F0393; NGA 28320.

name: Okha (Vomani Point, Humani Point)
tower: 23 m (75 ft) square cylindrical concrete tower with lantern and gallery, painted with horizontal red and white bands
colors: tower with lantern and gallery, painted with horizontal red and white bands
text: 1956. Active; focal plane 26 m (85 ft); three white flashes every 25 s. 23 m (75 ft) square cylindrical concrete tower with lantern and gallery, painted with horizontal red and white bands. Niraj Kumar has a photo. Google's satellite view shows the 60 m (197 ft) round VTS vessel tracking tower built next to the historic lighthouse in 2012. Wikimedia has a view taken from the VTS tower. Okha lies at the end of a north-pointing peninsula that defines the southern entrance to the Gulf of Kachchh (Kutch). After independence western India lost the use of the port of Karachi, Pakistan, so it became important to develop port facilities in the Gulf. This lighthouse was the first major improvement to navigational aids in this development. Located on Vomani (Humani) Point near the tip of the peninsula, adjacent to a historic fort. Site open, tower closed. ARLHS IND-014; Admiralty F0388; NGA 28312.

name: Samiyani Island (Okha Port)
light: flash every 5 s, white or red depending on direction
tower: 20 m (66 ft) round sandstone tower with lantern and gallery, mounted on a square stone base

text: 1876. Active; focal plane 22 m (72 ft); flash every 5 s, white or red depending on direction. 20 m (66 ft) round sandstone tower with lantern and gallery, mounted on a square stone base. Lighthouse painted white; lantern dome is red. A 2018 photo is at right, Kashyap Atri has a 2019 photo, Vishal Ahir has a 2024 view from the sea, and Google has a satellite view. Built by the princely state of Baroda, this elegant and historic lighthouse marks the entrance to Okha harbor. It stands on an island 1.5 km (1 mi) north of Okha Point, the tip of the peninsula. Boat transportation to the island can be hired in Okha. Located in the center of the island. Site open, tower closed. ARLHS IND-018; Admiralty F0390; NGA 28308.

name: Samiyani Island North
tower: 9 m (30 ft) round cylindrical concrete tower, mounted on a concrete foundation
colors: Lighthouse painted with black and white horizontal bands
text: 2002 (station established 1935). Active; focal plane 11 m (36 ft); green flash every 3 s. 9 m (30 ft) round cylindrical concrete tower, mounted on a concrete foundation. Lighthouse painted with black and white horizontal bands. Chetan Kanzariya has a distant view and Google has an indistinct satellite view. The original light on a skeletal tower was replaced by a concrete tower in 1957. That lighthouse was destroyed by a tropical cyclone on 9 June 1998. It was replaced by a temporary skeletal tower, and then by the present lighthouse, which probably resembles the 1957 tower. Located in the water off the northeast tip of Samiyani Island. , marking the end of a long shoal. Accessible only by boat. Site and tower closed. ARLHS IND-163; Admiralty F0389; NGA 28316.

name: Bural Reef (Chanka Reef)
tower: 12 m (39 ft) round cylindrical concrete tower with three galleries but no lantern, painted white
colors: tower with three galleries but no lantern, painted white
text: 1979. Active; focal plane 15 m (49 ft); quick-flashing white light. 12 m (39 ft) round cylindrical concrete tower with three galleries but no lantern, painted white. Lightphotos.net has an older photo, Indian Logistics Info.has a page with a photo, and Bing has a satellite view. The dangerous Bural Reef extends east northeast from Okha Point. Located about 25 km (15 mi) east northeast of Okha. Accessible only by boat. Site and tower closed. ARLHS IND-126; Admiralty F0386.5; NGA 28328.

name: Chank Tapu (Chanka Island)
tower: 8 m (26 ft) square cylindrical skeletal tower with gallery, mounted on a large square concrete base
colors: Lighthouse painted white; the small lantern is red
text: 1988 (station established 1934). Active; focal plane 14 m (46 ft); white flash every 15 s. 8 m (26 ft) square cylindrical skeletal tower with gallery, mounted on a large square concrete base. Wikimapia has an older photo and Bing has a satellite view. Lighthouse painted white; the small lantern is red. A stone daybeacon was placed on the reef in 1885; a skeletal tower was added in 1928 but apparently it was not lighted until 1934. Located at the northeastern end of the extensive Chanka Reef system, about 35 km (2 mi) east northeast of Okha. Accessible only by boat. Site and tower closed. Admiralty F0386; NGA 28332.

name: Kalubhar (Karumbhar) Island (Salaya)
tower: 20 m (66 ft) round stone tower with lantern and gallery, attached to a 1-story keeper's house
colors: Lighthouse painted white; lantern dome is red
text: 1884. Active; focal plane 27 m (89 ft); three white flashes every 15 s. 20 m (66 ft) round stone tower with lantern and gallery, attached to a 1-story keeper's house. Lighthouse painted white; lantern dome is red. Prashant Chauhan's 2020 photo is at right, Mukeshkumar Mali has a distant photo, and Google has a satellite view. This lighthouse, which marks the entrance to the harbor of Salaya, was built by the princely state of Nawanagar. The tower was restored and increased in height in 1961. Located just off the west end of the island about 20 km (12.5 mi) north of Salaya. Accessible only by boat. Site and tower closed. ARLHS IND-169; Admiralty F0384; NGA 28336.

name: Pathfinder Inlet (Vadinar) Range Front (2 towers)
text: 2015 (station established 2008). Active; focal plane unknown; continuous red light. Mast atop a tall square skeletal tower, height unknown. No photo available but Google has a satellite view. The new port of Vadinar serves area oil refineries. The satellite view shows a second tower just to the north; it's not clear if this is the inactive original tower or if it is an active auxiliary light. Located a short distance south of the port area. Accessible only by boat. Site open, tower closed. Operator: Deendayal Port Trust. Admiralty F0383.75.

name: Pathfinder Inlet (Vadinar) Range Rear (2 towers)
text: 2015 (station established 2008). Active; focal plane unknown; flashing white light. Mast atop a tall square skeletal tower, height unknown. No photo available but Google has a satellite view. The satellite view shows a second tower just to the north; it's not clear if this is the inactive original tower or if it is an active auxiliary light. Located 750 m (1/2 mi) south of the front light. Accessible only by boat. Site open, tower closed. Operator: Deendayal Port Trust. Admiralty F0383.751.

name: Sikka Range Front (2?)
text: 2011. Active; focal plane unknown; continuous red light. Skeletal tower atop a square platform supported by piles. No photo available but Google has a distant satellite view. Sikka is a traditional fishing port that now also hosts several industrial plants. The range lights were moved about 500 m (0.3 mi) southeast in 2021. Located a short distance east of the pier at Sikka. Accessible only by boat. Site open, tower closed. Operator: Sikka Ports and Terminals. Admiralty F0382.51; NGA 28347.

name: Sikka Range Rear (2?)
text: 2011. Active; focal plane unknown; continuous red light. Skeletal tower atop a square platform supported by piles. No photo available but Google has a distant satellite view. Located 500 m (1/3 mi) southeast of the front light. Accessible only by boat. Site open, tower closed. Operator: Sikka Ports and Terminals. Admiralty F0382.511; NGA 28347.5.

name: Pirotan (Pirothan) Island
tower: 21 m (69 ft) round masonry tower with lantern and gallery, painted with horizontal black and white bands
colors: tower with lantern and gallery, painted with horizontal black and white bands
text: 1958 (station established 1898). Active; focal plane 26 m (85 ft); white flash every 20 s. 21 m (69 ft) round masonry tower with lantern and gallery, painted with horizontal black and white bands. Jayesh Kumar's 2020 photo is at right, Wikimedia has a sunrise photo by S. Ballal, Kumar has another 2020 photo, and Google has a satellite view. A seawall protects this highly exposed lighthouse. Pirotan is the beginning of the approach to Bedi, the seaport of the city of Jamnagar. Located on a small island 10 km (6 mi) northwest of Rozi. Accessible only by boat. Site and tower closed. ARLHS IND-157; Admiralty F0380; NGA 28352.

name: Mawadi Point (Pirotan Northeast)
tower: 8 m (26 ft) short round tower mounted atop a round cylindrical stone tower

text: 1958 (station established 1928). Active; focal plane 8 m (26 ft); red flash every 10 s. 8 m (26 ft) short round tower mounted atop a round cylindrical stone tower. The upper tower is painted red with a white horizontal band. The lower tower is unpainted brown stone. Tushar Chhatrara has a photo but the light is not shown in Google's satellite view. The light marks the end of a reef extending northeast from Pirotan Island. The first light was a skeletal tower built on a daybecaon established in 1867. Located about 2.25 km (1.4 mi) northeast of the modern lighthouse. Site open, and nothing prevents climbing on the lighthouse. Admiralty F0378; NGA 28356.

name: Rozi Port (Bedi Bandar, Bedi Bundar, Bedi)
tower: 25 m (82 ft) round cylindrical vessel traffic control tower painted with red and white horizontal bands
colors: tower painted with red and white horizontal bands
text: Date unknown. Inactive since 2002. Approx. 25 m (82 ft) round cylindrical vessel traffic control tower painted with red and white horizontal bands. Hari Prasad Kanithi has a 2018 photo, a 2016 photo (first photo on the page) is available, Tanmay Vora has a 2012 view from across the harbor, and Google has a satellite view. This tower replaced a 12 m (39 ft) square skeletal tower with a small equipment closet in the base. The light was deactivated because it became redundant on the brightly lit Rozi Pier. Located on the quay at Bedi Bandar, the seaport serving the city of Jamnagar. Site open, tower closed. ARLHS IND-124; ex-Admiralty F0376; ex-NGA 28358.

name: Rozi (Rojhi)
tower: 13 m (43 ft) round cylindrical stone tower, a bastion at the northwest corner of the fortified Rozi Mata temple, now in ruins
text: 1867. Inactive since 1976. Approx. 13 m (43 ft) round cylindrical stone tower, a bastion at the northwest corner of the fortified Rozi Mata temple, now in ruins. Sandeepsinh Sodha has a photo and Google has a satellite view. The original light was on a mast atop the tower; in 1897 it was replaced by a "cast iron pedestal" with a 6th order Fresnel lens. The light was moved to the new Rozi Pier in 1976. Located just east of the base of the pier. Site open, tower status unknown.

name: Mungra Reef
tower: 10 m (33 ft) round cylindrical concrete tower on a circular masonry pier
colors: Tower painted red with one white horizontal band
text: 1890 (rebuilt and lit in 1997; rebuilt a second time in 1999). Active; focal plane 10 m (33 ft); two white flashes every 10 s. 10 m (33 ft) round cylindrical concrete tower on a circular masonry pier. Tower painted red with one white horizontal band. The Indian Logistics Info photo is at right, but the light is not seen in Bing's satellite view. The lighthouse marks a dangerous reef on the approach to Jodiya Bandar. The native state of Nawanagar built this beacon. It was rebuilt in 1999 after being heavily damaged by a tropical cyclone on 9 June 1998. Located in the Gulf of Kachchh about 12 km (7.5 mi) northwest of Jodiya Bandar. Accessible only by boat. Site and tower closed. ARLHS IND-151; Admiralty F0367.8; NGA 28366.

name: Jodiya (Jodia) Bandar

text: 2002 (station established 1903). Active; focal plane 31 m (102 ft); white flash every 10 s. 30 m (98 ft) skeletal tower, painted white. A 2021 photo and a distant 2025 view are available and Google has a satellite view. The 1993 lighthouse, a round cylindrical masonry tower with gallery attached to a small square 1-story equipment room, was destroyed by the earthquake of 26 January 2001. The original lighthouse was a small cast iron tower purchased from Chance Brothers by the native state of Nawanagar. Located at Jodiya (Jodia), a small port on the upper Gulf of Kachchh. Site open, tower closed. ARLHS IND-141; Admiralty F0368; NGA 28368.

name: Navlakhi (Navlakhi Bet, Kandla Port)
tower: 30 m (98 ft) round concrete tower with lantern, gallery, and an observation level, very similar to the Bhadreswar lighthouse at right
colors: Tower painted with horizontal red and white bands
text: 2012 (station established 1932). Active; focal plane 30 m (198 ft); three white flashes every 10 s. 30 m (98 ft) round concrete tower with lantern, gallery, and an observation level, very similar to the Bhadreswar lighthouse at right. Tower painted with horizontal red and white bands. Saiad Sekh has a 2023 photo, Rajesh Shah has a distant view, and Google has a satellite view. The light guides ships approaching the port facility at Navlakhi at the head of the Gulf of Kachchh. The original light was replaced in 1985 by a 24 m (79 ft) skeletal tower. That lighthouse was knocked out of service by the earthquake of 26 January 2001, but it was restored and returned to service the following month. Located on the northwestern tip of Navlakhi Island. Accessible only by boat. Site and tower closed. ARLHS IND-155; Admiralty F0370; NGA 28376.

name: Tekra (Tuna) (3?)
colors: tower, painted with black and white horizontal bands
text: Date unknown (station established 1892). Active; focal plane 17 m (56 ft); white flash every 7 s. Formerly described as a 14 m (46) "metal column" atop a masonry tower, painted with black and white horizontal bands. The light is now described by NGA as a "metal column" with black and white horizontal bands. No photo available and Google now has a satellite view showing what appears to be a round concrete tower. The light guides ships entering Kandla Port, a greatly expanded port facility at the head of the Gulf of Kachchh. The original light was described as an "iron column." Located on the west side of a creek entrance in the Kandla Port complex south of Anjar, near the head of the Gulf of Kachchh. Site status unknown. Operator: Adanai Ports Tuna Terminal. Admiralty F0366; NGA 28380.

name: Bhadreswar (Nakti Creek)
tower: 60 m (197 ft) round concrete tower with lantern and double gallery

A 2023 photo is at right and Google has a satellite view. This light is mounted on a vessel traffic control tower. Located at Bhadreswar, a village about 30 km (19 mi) northwest of Mundra. name: #Mundra New Port (Mitha Port)
text: 1985 (station established 1951). Inactive since 2011 and probably demolished. This was a 7 m (23 ft) square cylindrical concrete column attached to a 1-story concrete equipment room. No photo available and Google's satellite view does not show the light. A new port, sheltered from the summer monsoon winds, was developed at Mundra during the 1950s. In 1998-2001 a major new Mundra Port was developed by private interests. The original lighthouse was a skeletal tower. Located on the Mitha quay, a small boat quay within the Mundra port area. Site open, tower closed. ARLHS IND-150; ex-Admiralty F0364; ex-NGA 28400.

Admiralty F0361.81; NGA 28398.5.

The NGA listing for Navinal Point is confused; it has the location of this light but the description "White structure, black bands" fits the traffic control tower (next entry). This was a temporary location for the light after the second (1965) lighthouse had to be removed for devlopment of the port. Located on the waterfront of the port. Site and tower closed. ex-Admiralty F0362; NGA 28396.

name: #Rawal Pir
colors: Lighthouse painted white
text: 1969 (station established 1936). Inactive since 2020 and apparently demolished. This was a 7 m (23 ft) square cylindrical concrete column attached to a 1-story concrete equipment room. Lighthouse painted white. Tarak Shanishchara's 2024 photo, taken from the top of the current lighthouse, does not show the older light. The original light was mounted on the tomb of a revered Sufi master (known as a pir). A separate tower was provided in 1947 and replaced in 1969. Located close to the Ravdpir (Rawal Pir) Temple complex about 3 km (2 mi) east of Mandvi. Site open, tower closed. ARLHS IND-160.

name: Rawal Pir
tower: 31 m (102 ft) round concrete tower with lantern and two galleries painted with red and white spiral bands

Active; focal plane 40 m (131 ft); green flash every 3 s. 31 m (102 ft) round concrete tower with lantern and two galleries painted with red and white spiral bands. Admiralty F0360; NGA 28404.

name: Mandvi Breakwater
tower: 7 m (23 ft) square cylindrical concrete tower, upper half painted red and lower half white
colors: tower, upper half painted red and lower half white
text: 1957 (station established 1890). Active; focal plane 8 m (26 ft); red flash every 3 s. 7 m (23 ft) square cylindrical concrete tower, upper half painted red and lower half white. Sahil Rayma has a 2017 photo and a 2020 photo, Parth Parmar has a photo showing the lighthouse in silhouette, Chandresh Malamwala has a distant view, Aresh Hirani has a street view across the harbor entrance, and Google has a satellite view. name: #Mandvi (Mandvi Fort)
visit: Site open, status of the fortress tower unknown.
text: 1964 (station established 1856). Demolished in 2001. This was a round cylindrical tower with lantern and gallery mounted on a round stone tower 17th century fortress of Mandvi; the light was listed with a focal plane of 35 m (115 ft). Google has a satellite view of the fortress. Heavily damaged in the earthquake of 26 January 2001, the lighthouse was pulled down the following month. Located on the south side of the new lighthouse. Site open, status of the fortress tower unknown.

name: Mandvi
light: three white flashes, separated by 5 s, every 30 s
tower: 30 m (98 ft) round cylindrical concrete vessel traffic control tower with two circular observation levels
colors: Lighthouse painted with red and white horizontal bands
visit: Site open, tower probably open but we have no information on this.
text: 2012 (station established 1856). Active; focal plane 63 m (207 ft); three white flashes, separated by 5 s, every 30 s. 30 m (98 ft) round cylindrical concrete vessel traffic control tower with two circular observation levels. Lighthouse painted with red and white horizontal bands. Hitendra Vankani's 2024 photo is at right, Tanmay Vora has a closeup photo, Hardik Dhayani has a 2015 photo, Vinay Toprani has a photo, and Google has a 2023 street view and a satellite view. The 1964 lighthouse (previous entry) was a cylindrical concrete tower with lantern and gallery; that lighthouse was demolished after being heavily damaged by the earthquake of 26 January 2001. It was replaced by a skeletal tower until the present tower was built. Mandvi has been the major port of the Kachchh district for many centuries. The lighthouse is built on the historic Mandvi Fort, from which lights were often displayed when friendly ships were expected. Although DGLL dates the modern light station to 1873, Ken Trethewey's research indicated that the British built a lighthouse on the fort in 1856. Light lists indicate that a taller tower was built in 1889. Located near the waterfront in Mandvi. Site open, tower probably open but we have no information on this. ARLHS IND-145; Admiralty F0357; NGA 28411.

name: Chhachhi (Kachchigadh)
tower: 31 m (102 ft) square cylindrical masonry tower with lantern and gallery
colors: Lighthouse painted with horizontal black and white bands; lantern roof painted red
visit: Site open, although roads in the area are poor; tower closed.
text: 1964 (station established 1957). Active; focal plane 33 m (108 ft); three white flashes every 15 s. 31 m (102 ft) square cylindrical masonry tower with lantern and gallery. Lighthouse painted with horizontal black and white bands; lantern roof painted red. DGLL's photo shows the lighthouse and the much taller traffic control tower that has stood next to it since 2008. Saurabh Parmar has a 2019 photo of the two towers, Niraj Kumar also has a photo, and Google has a satellite view of the two towers. This is an important lighthouse marking the northern entrance to the Gulf of Kachchh. Located near the village of Chhachhi about 50 km (30 mi) north northwest of Mandvi. Site open, although roads in the area are poor; tower closed. ARLHS IND-015; Admiralty F0356; NGA 28416.

name: Jakhau
tower: 41 m (135 ft) round cylindrical concrete tower with lantern and gallery, painted with horizontal red and white bands
colors: tower with lantern and gallery, painted with horizontal red and white bands
text: 1965 (station established 1957). Active; focal plane 46 m (151 ft); white flash every 10 s. 41 m (135 ft) round cylindrical concrete tower with lantern and gallery, painted with horizontal red and white bands. Prashant Chauhan's 2024 photo is at right, Chandrakant Swain has a 2018 photo, DGLL has a photo of the 60 m (197 ft) traffic control tower that stands next to the lighthouse, Chandrakant Swain has a photo of both towers, and Google has a satellite view. The original lighthouse here was replaced in 1964. Located on the main quay of Jakhau, a fishing port in western Kachchh. Site open, tower closed. ARLHS IND-138; Admiralty F0355; NGA 28420.

name: Koteshwar
tower: 57 m (187 ft) round cylindrical concrete tower with lantern and gallery, painted with black and white horizontal bands
colors: tower with lantern and gallery, painted with black and white horizontal bands
text: 2014 (?). Active; focal plane 60 m (197 ft); two white flashes every 15 s. Approx. 57 m (187 ft) round cylindrical concrete tower with lantern and gallery, painted with black and white horizontal bands. Jay Thakker has a 2023 photo, Tanmay Vora has a photo, Lightphotos.net has a photo, and Google has a satellite view. This is both the northernmost and the westernmost lighthouse of India. It has strategic value, standing to the east of the disputed Rann of Kutch area on the Pakistani frontier. Located on the south side of the village of Koteshwar facing the inlet known as Kori Creek. Site open, tower closed. Admiralty F0354; NGA 28420.5.

name: Umargam (Umergaon, Umbergaon)
tower: 30 m (98 ft) triangular cylindrical concrete tower with lantern and double gallery, painted with horizontal red and white bands
colors: tower with lantern and double gallery, painted with horizontal red and white bands
text: 1979. Active; focal plane 35 m (115 ft); white flash every 15 s. 30 m (98 ft) triangular cylindrical concrete tower with lantern and double gallery, painted with horizontal red and white bands. Khalasi Krunal's 2019 photo is at the top of this page, Vikas Mhaskar has a 2021 photo, Chandni Rajendran has a view from atop the lighthouse, and Google has a satellite view. Umergam Beach is a popular resort, and the lighthouse is an attraction. Located off the beach at Umbergaon. Site open, tower open daily. Operator: DGLL. ARLHS IND-118; Admiralty F0489; NGA 28092.

name: Maroli
tower: 5 m (41 ft); white flash every 1
text: Date unknown. Active (?); focal plane 12.5 m (41 ft); white flash every 1.5 s. 11 m (36 ft) square skeletal tower. Google has a street view and Bing has an indistinct satellite view, but the lighthouse looks abandoned in the street view. Located at the edge of the beach in Maroli, a town about 11 km (7 mi) north of Umbergaon. Site open, tiwer closed. Admiralty F0488; NGA 28096.

name: Daman (1) (Damão, Rio Sandalcalo)
tower: 10 m (33 ft) round masonry tower with gallery and a small light on a post
colors: Lighthouse painted white
text: 1884 (Portuguese). Inactive since 1999. Approx. 10 m (33 ft) round masonry tower with gallery and a small light on a post. Lighthouse painted white. Long in deteriorating condition, the historic lighthouse was recently restored and repainted, as seen in JSnehal Hemant Jadhav's 2022 photo at right. Wikimedia has a 2013 closeup, Monica Reis has a 2007 photo, Vishvesh Chauhan has a photo also showing the new lighthouse, Divyeshkumar Shukla has a 2017 street view, and Google has a satellite view. The Daman lighthouses are associated with a 16th century Portuguese fort, Forte Moti Daman, one of the best known tourist attractions of the territory. Located just inside the outer wall of the fort, on the south side of the entrance to the Daman Ganga River. . ARLHS IND-129.

name: Daman (Daman Ganga)

Hazira, at the southern entrance to the Gulf of Khambhat, was one of the first British light stations in India; the 20 m (66 ft) round stone tower completed in 1836 was replaced by a 27 m (90 ft) round brick tower in 1867. Today Hazira is being developed as a major port facility to relieve pressure on the overcrowded piers of Mumbai. Located on a promontory on the north side of the entrance to the Tapti River estuary from the Gulf, about 30 km (19 mi) southwest of Surat. Accessible by road. Site open, tower closed. Operator: DGLL. ARLHS IND-136; Admiralty F0476; NGA 28120.

name: Ruvapari (Ruvapori)
text: 1922 (station established 1891). Active (?); focal plane 20 m (66 ft); white flash every 12 s. Square 1-story wood keeper's house with a pyramidal corrugated iron roof, mounted on Burmese teak pilings. Since 1994 the light has been shown from the top of a tall mast mounted on the roof. A DGLL photo is at right and Google has a satellite view; in both views the lighthouse appears high and dry on mud flats. The original lighthouse was destroyed by a tropical cyclone in 1920. The survival of this old-fashioned pile lighthouse is astonishing. The Indian Quarterly had an article by Ramesh Menon (no longer online) stating that the lighthouse has a resident keeper. The 16 teak straightpiles are about 450 mm (18 in) in diameter. Located on the south side of the entrance to what is now the Bhavnagar New Port, about 11 km (7 mi) east of the town. It may be possible to walk to the lighthouse, but this doesn't appear to be a very attractive option. Site open, tower closed. Operator: DGLL. ARLHS IND-162; Admiralty F0456; NGA 28156.

The station was inaugurated in 1856 with a mast light; this was replaced by a cast iron tower in 1887 and then by a masonry tower in 1936. Another tower was built in 1961. (We need more information about the history of this station!) Although Ghogha is a minor port the present lighthouse functions mostly as an approach light for Bhavnagar. Located on the west side of the Gulf of Khambhat at Ghogha, about 22 km (14 mi) southeast of Bhavnagar. Site open, tower closed. Operator: DGLL. ARLHS IND-134; Admiralty F0452; NGA 28176.

Entire vessel painted red. A DGLL photo is at right and Bing has a satellite view. This vessel, the third to serve on the station, marks a dangerous shoal in the channel on the approach to Bhavnagar. Operated as an automated lightfloat, the ship was reported still on station in 2010. Located 3 km (2 mi) northeast of the Ghogha lighthouse; there should be a distant view from the Ghogha waterfront. Site and vessel closed. Operator: DGLL. ARLHS IND-144; Admiralty F0449; NGA 28184.

The island is privately owned and available for purchase or development. Located on the southwest side of the island, about 10 km (6 mi) southeast of Ghogha. Accessible only by boat. The Vengurla Rocks are bare rocks best known as a breeding site for a rare bird, the Indian swiftlet. Located on the westernmost reef of the Vengurla Rocks about 800 m (1/2 mi) west of the 1890 lighthouse. Accessible only by boat and landing appears difficult or impossible. Site and tower closed.

In late 2005 and early 2006 the exterior of the lighthouse was patched and painted white, as seen in a March 2006 photo. This was an improvement but Vineeth K. Bhat's May 2007 photo shows the lighthouse quickly reverting to its weathered appearance. Early in 2008 the lighthouse was once again patched and painted, but by December it was weathering again, as seen in Biplab Narendra's photo. Ankit Khanna's June 2010 photo shows another repainting and Pankaj Anand's August 2012 photo shows another cycle of weathering. The two lighthouses of Fort Aguada were paired as a range during the early 20th century. Located in Fort Aguada, an early 16th century Portuguese fortification, about 10 km (6 mi) west of Panaji. We need more information on the history of this interesting tower. An article in Wikipedia says the tower was built as a watchtower by Sultan Haidar Ali, the de facto ruler of the Mysore kingdom from about 1763 until his death in 1782; if so, the tower dates from that era. The British annexed Mangalore in 1799. Findlay's 1879 light list gives 1870 as the establishment of a modern light; from its hilltop location the light had a focal plane of 73 m (240 ft). There exist historic images (third and fourth rows on the page) that show something like a conventional lantern room atop the tower; one image is dated 1905. The 1904 world light list does not include the light. Located in Tagore Park, atop Light House Hill above the business district of Mangalore. Site open, tower closed. ARLHS IND-171.

In early 2020 a plan was approved for a more complete $500,000 restoration leading to opening the lighthouse as a tourist attraction. Work on the project began in November 2020 but was slowed by the pandemic; the photo at right and an October 2022 photo show the completed work. Located on the sea front in Puducherry. text: Date unknown (station established 1898). Active; focal plane unknown; quick-flashing white light. The light lists do not describe this light. The listed location, also charted by C-Map, is at or near the Diamond Harbor passenger ferry terminal. Pradipta Jana's photo of the ferry wharf shows a tall mast rising from a square base about 6 m (20 ft) tall; this is a possible location for the light. Google has an indistinct satellite view. Diamond Harbour is on the east side of the Hooghly on the southern edge of the Kolkata metropolitan area. It has no port facilities but it was a protected anchorage for ships waiting to proceed to the city's docks. In 1904 the light was listed with a focal plane of 14 m (46 ft). A note is in order here concerning persistent reports of a historic Diamond Harbour lighthouse. Numerous Indian web sites repeat the claim that there is an "old lighthouse" close to a ruined Portuguese fort in Diamond Harbour. The fort ruins are real but they have washed into the river in recent years. A frequently posted historic engraving of a "Diamond Point" lighthouse is almost certainly an image of the lost Cowcolly (Kaukhali) lighthouse on the other side of the estuary. As best one can determine there was never a European-style light station at Diamond Harbour (nor would there have been a need for one). Active (?); focal plane 35 m (115 ft); two white flashes every 20 s. 35 m (115 ft) round cast iron tower with lantern and gallery, painted with red and white spiral stripes. 3rd order Fresnel lens in use. A 2024 photo is at right, Lightphotos.net has a 2013 aerial photo, Mohammed Ramees has a 2018 photo, and Google has a satellite view. Marking the southernmost point of Indian territory, this lighthouse is an important landmark for ships bound to or from the Strait of Malacca. The point of land, formerly called Parsons Point and later Pygmalion Point, was renamed Indira Point after Prime Minister Indira Gandhi made a visit to the light station. A monument to her has been placed to mark the point. The tsunami of December 26, 2004, swept away all the structures of the station except the lighthouse. 16 people were killed, including the keepers and a number of scientists who happened to be visiting at the time. Geologists later estimated that the land in the area subsided 4.5 m (almost 15 ft) as a result of the earthquake that caused the tsunami; this subsidence left the lighthouse standing in the water, where it is clearly endangered. Nonetheless, the Indian Coast Guard succeeded in reactivating the lighthouse by the end of February 2005. When the light failed in 2007 the repair crew could not reach the tower from land, so they were lowered to the tower by helicopter. The January 2018 photo at right shows that sand has washed around the base of the tower, bringing it just barely onto the beach at low tide. Located at the southern tip of Great Nicobar Island; the station is said to be accessible by road. Site open, tower closed. ARLHS AND-007; Admiralty F1224; NGA 26424.
